item.title: Incarico post-doc: Incarico Post-Doc - GIUR-14/A - Restorative Justice in the Regional Context of Friuli Venezia Giulia: Critical Issues and Prospects Based on Legal Practice Experience (Univ. TRIESTE)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-16 23:59
Institution: Univ. TRIESTE, Trieste
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-14 Diritto penale

This research project addresses the implementation of restorative justice within the Italian legal system, with particular attention to the regional context of Friuli Venezia Giulia. Building on a systematic and critical reconstruction of the framework introduced by Legislative Decree No. 150/2022 – in its substantive, procedural, and organizational dimensions – the research extends to an empirical field investigation, conducted through semi-structured interviews with criminal defense lawyers and judges operating in the region. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Digital innovation in territorial governance (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-06 Diritto amministrativo e pubblico

The research addresses the legal aspects of digital innovation, with specific reference to their application to territorial governance. It will examine in depth the European and national legal frameworks governing artificial intelligence, in order to assess the prerequisites and limits of applicability of AI systems within public administration, with a primary focus on the urban planning and building sectors.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Commercial Law in the Papal States of the Restoration: The Provisional Regulation of 1821 Between the Napoleonic Legacy and the ius commune (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Law / 12/GIUR-16 Storia del diritto medievale e moderno

This research will analyze papal commercial law during the Restoration era, examining the impact of Napoleonic legislation on common law beginning with the 1821 Regulation. The study will examine the debate on commercial jurisdiction, codification projects, and university teaching in Rome. Based on archival sources and contemporary legal scholarship, the study aims to chart the comparison between the “mos italicus” and the French school. The ultimate goal is a comprehensive reconstruction of the system, complete with a bibliography of sources and scholarly publications
